text.p: British drug company Glaxo Wellcome Plc rose on Thursday to highlight trade in American Deposity Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said European ADRs were mostly stronger on the back of home exchanges following New York markets higher and because of a sliding dollar.

Glaxo rose 3/4 to 33-5/8 in heavy volume after the company announced an 18 percent jump in 1996 pretax profits. The company warned of a more difficult next two years after this July's expiration of the U.S. patent for its best-selling drug, the anti-ulcer treatment Zantac.
Analysts backed Glaxo's prediction it would return to double-digit sales growth by the end of the century.
Among other European ADRs, Swedish telecommunications supplier Ericsson rose 5/8 to 34 and Italian luxury goods dealer Gucci rose 1-1/8 to 68-5/8.
Italian telephone holding company Stet SpA went up 1-1/8 to 45-1/8 following an Italian newspaper report it was planning an alliance with the United States' AT&T Corp.
Stet denied the report and an AT&T spokesman said the company's policy was not to comment on rumors or speculation.

The report in financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the alliance could involve either Stet entering the Unisource consortium, which Spain's Telefonica de Espana would leave, or the two groups creating a new consortium to take part in the privatization of Brazil's Telebras.
Telebras was up 1-1/8 to 102-3/4 and Telefonica rose 7/8 to 70-1/8.
Advancers led decliners by 271 to 201 among 806 ADRs. Volume was 40 million shares at midday.
